item.title: JavaScript in the Browser: Where the Request Begins
item.description: Every backend request starts with a line of JavaScript in a browser. Here's what actually happens before a single byte hits the network.

item.title: HTTP and Networking: The Request Hits the Wire
item.description: DNS, TCP's handshake, TLS, and what an HTTP request actually looks like as bytes on the wire.

item.title: Linux: Process, Socket, and Nginx
item.description: How the Linux kernel turns a stream of bytes into something a server process can read, and why nginx sits in front of Java almost everywhere.

item.title: Java and the JVM: Threads and Spring
item.description: The request lands in a thread pool, a DispatcherServlet routes it, and the JVM does a surprising amount of work you never asked for.

item.title: SQL: Connection, Transaction, and Index
item.description: The request finally touches data: a pooled connection, a transaction boundary, and the index that decides if the query takes 2ms or 2s.
